conflicts.fact: Whether first ionisation energy increases across Period 3 and what the Al value is; the Lesson 6 explanation of Al not reacting relies on a higher ionisation energy than Mg
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 says IE generally increases across Period 3 with a dip at Al (outer electron in 3p, more easily removed than Mg's). Lesson 6 gives Al IE = 577, lower than Mg = 738, but then explains that Al and Si do not react with cold water because they have 'even higher effective nuclear charges and higher ionisation energies', which contradicts Al's lower IE in its own data.

conflicts.fact: Observed pH of the alkaline solutions and the flame colour/observations used as the benchmark; also the Group II cold water pH values vs the claim that Mg barely reacts
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 gives pH 8 to 14 for Group I solutions (an implausible lower bound for hydroxides of Li/Na/K, which would all be strongly alkaline). Lesson 3 says Mg in cold water gives pH ~9-10.

conflicts.fact: Sodium's product gas and flame: whether the hydrogen ignites and how it was tested
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 and 7 say sodium ignites with an orange flame (Lesson 7 says hydrogen ignites). Lesson 6 says the gas burned with a pop (colourless gas), and Lesson 3 uses a squeaky pop with a lighted splint for Mg/HCl; Lesson 2 uses a glowing splint to test hydrogen, which would not relight.

conflicts.fact: Lesson 4 says the argon inertness is the extreme end of the 'electron gain' trend; reactivity of halogens and explanation of why chlorine is used; also Lesson 4 says electron affinity explains Group VII while Lesson 7 says electronegativity/oxidising power
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 claims chlorine's reactivity trend is due to electron affinity and that it is used because it has the highest electron affinity among Cl, Br, I (though fluorine is also given in the scaffold). Lesson 7 attributes chlorine's disinfecting power to high electronegativity, and Lesson 5/7 define argon's inertness as having no tendency to gain or lose electrons, not as the end of a Period 3 electron-gain trend.

conflicts.fact: Role of sodium storage: argon ampoule vs mineral oil
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says sodium is stored under mineral oil and the argon ampoule is merely demonstrated as inert. Lessons 2, 5 and 7 state that the officer stored/transported the sodium in argon; Lesson 2 attributes this to sodium's outer electron being lost to trace moisture in air.

conflicts.fact: Density trend of Group I metals
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says density 'generally increases' down Group I (Li, Na, K); in reality K (0.86) is less dense than Na (0.97), so the stated trend conflicts with the actual data the class would receive, and Lesson 2 asks about density of Li floating.

conflicts.fact: Number of inner shielding electrons / shielding description for sodium
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says sodium has '2 full inner shells providing moderate shielding' with 11 protons; Lesson 7 says shielded by 10 inner electrons; for Mg Lesson 7 says shielded by 10 inner electrons with +12 charge, consistent, but Lesson 5 says shielding 'remains nearly constant' while Lesson 7 says it is the 'same shielding effect' — consistent; no conflict beyond wording.
